sections.h2: Which Maricopa County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The county splits the job between an assessor and a treasurer. The Maricopa County Assessor values property, classifies it and mails the annual Notice of Value. The Maricopa County Treasurer bills and collects real and personal property taxes for more than 1,800 tax districts, including the state, county, cities and towns, schools, community colleges and special districts, then distributes the money to them.

  • Treasurer: 301 West Jefferson Street, Suite 100, Phoenix, AZ 85003. Office hours 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Customer service 602-506-8511.
  • Assessor: 602-506-3406.
  • Parcel search and online payment run through the Treasurer's site, and the eNotices program offers paperless bills with an authorization code printed on your tax bill.

The Treasurer's site warns about mail, text and phone scams that push alternate payment methods. Pay only through the county's own site or the address on your bill.

sections.h2: What is Maricopa County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Maricopa County is the biggest county in Arizona by a wide margin. It covers 9,224 square miles, stretching 132 miles west to east, and had 4,420,568 people in the 2020 census, about 62% of the state. The 2020 count also showed 1,812,827 housing units with 9.3% vacant, and 63.0% of occupied homes were owner-occupied. Phoenix is the seat, and the county holds fifteen cities and ten towns, including Mesa, Chandler, Scottsdale, Tempe and Gilbert.

The county also contains a mix of school districts, from unified districts such as Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert and Scottsdale to union high school and elementary districts in Phoenix and the West Valley. Because each district, city, fire district and special district levies its own rate, two houses with the same value can have different bills. Look up your parcel rather than relying on a neighbor's number.

Five Indian reservations lie inside the county, the largest being the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community and the Gila River Indian Community. Property on reservation land follows different rules, and the Assessor can tell you whether a parcel is on the roll.

sections.h2: When is Maricopa County property tax due?
sections.html:
Under A.R.S. 42-18052, half the tax is due October 1 and the other half the following March 1. Unpaid halves become delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and May 1. A bill of $100 or less is due in full on October 1 and is delinquent after December 31. If a delinquency date lands on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day.

DateEvent
October 1, 2026First-half 2026 taxes due
November 2, 2026, after 5 p.m.First half delinquent (passed)
December 1Final delinquent notices for unpaid 2025 taxes
December 31, 2026Last day to pay 2026 full-year taxes over $100 without interest
March 1, 2027Second half due
May 1, 2027, 5 p.m.Second half delinquent

Source: Maricopa County Treasurer calendar and A.R.S. 42-18052.

May 1, 2027 is a Saturday, so under subsection D the delinquency time moves to 5:00 p.m. on the next business day. Paying the full year on or before December 31 avoids interest under A.R.S. 42-18053. Otherwise unpaid tax bears 16% a year, simple, and a part of a month counts as a whole month.

sections.h2: How does the Maricopa County tax lien process work?
sections.html:
The Treasurer publishes an annual calendar for delinquent accounts. Delinquent taxes are assessed an advertising fee in January, and an online tax lien auction takes place in February. Late in the spring a second-half bill goes delinquent on May 1, and first delinquent notices go out in June. Bidders may begin buying the current delinquent year after that. A second round of delinquent notices goes out in December.

A buyer at the auction receives a certificate of purchase and not a deed. The Treasurer's calendar notes that December 31 is the final day to purchase subsequent taxes and assignments. For a seller the message is simple: do not let the first half sit unpaid into the new year.

The lien itself comes from A.R.S. 42-17153. It attaches on January 1 of the tax year, ranks ahead of other private liens, and stays until the tax, interest and charges are paid, title vests in a purchaser at a tax sale, or a certificate of removal and abatement issues. A title company will want the lien cleared from your sale proceeds.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Maricopa County property value?
sections.html:
The Assessor must mail a Notice of Value between January 1 and March 1 each year. If you think the full cash value or the legal class is wrong, file a Petition for Review of Real Property Valuation with the Assessor within 60 days after the mailing date. Owners or their representatives can file online. The Assessor's handout also says the appeal covers full cash value and classification, not the limited property value.

  • Assessor level: answers are due by mid-August in the handout's example year. The 2026 notice went out February 21, 2025, with an April 22, 2025 filing deadline.
  • State Board of Equalization: file within 25 days of the Assessor's decision. The board hears both sides before an officer.
  • Superior Court: tax court or small claims, filed by December 15 of the notice year, or within 60 days of the latest administrative decision. Small claims covers owner-occupied residential property and any property valued under $2 million.

The handout explains that limited property value is the only value used to compute tax and rises at most 5% a year unless the property changes through additions, deletions or a change in use. A buyer who acquires a house after December 15 can appeal to court if the prior owner did not. The statutory 60-day rule is in A.R.S. 42-16051.

sections.h2: What relief programs does the Maricopa County Assessor offer?
sections.html:
The Assessor's homepage lists veteran personal exemptions for the 100% service-connected disability exemption, and a notice dated June 24, 2026 says changes to the disabled veterans' exemptions arrive in 2027 as part of the state budget. A September 21, 2026 article summarizes legislative changes from the 2026 session that affect owners and veterans. Read those pages before you rely on an older rule.

The office also takes rental registrations online and holds virtual appointments. For widow, widower, disability and senior-valuation programs, ask the Assessor for current forms and limits. Dollar limits and deadlines for these programs change from year to year.

sections.h2: What happens to tax when you sell a Maricopa County house?
sections.html:
The deed gets recorded and the Assessor updates ownership, but the lien for the current tax year already exists from January 1. At closing, the title company asks the Treasurer for what is owed and pays it from proceeds. If you sell in the fall, it matters whether the first half was paid. If you sell after December 31 with the full year unpaid, interest at 16% a year is already counted from the delinquency dates.

Foreclosure sales that bring in more than the debt can leave money behind. Maricopa County's Treasurer lists excess proceeds that a foreclosing attorney deposited under A.R.S. 33-812 on the Treasurer's website.

faqs.q: When is the Maricopa County property tax deadline in 2026?
faqs.a: The first half of 2026 tax was due October 1 and became delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 2, 2026. Full-year 2026 taxes over $100 can still be paid without interest through December 31, 2026. The second half is due March 1, 2027.

faqs.q: How much interest does Maricopa County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: Delinquent tax bears 16% interest a year, simple, from the delinquency date, and a fraction of a month counts as a whole month, under A.R.S. 42-18053. No interest is collected if the full year is paid by December 31 or if the delinquency came from an assessor or treasurer error.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Maricopa County Notice of Value?
faqs.a: You have 60 days after the Assessor mailed the notice. File a Petition for Review of Real Property Valuation with the Assessor, online or on paper. If you disagree with the result, the State Board of Equalization takes appeals within 25 days of the Assessor's decision.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Maricopa County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Treasurer's customer service at 602-506-8511 for amounts due and payments. Call the Assessor at 602-506-3406 about value, classification and exemptions. The Treasurer's office is at 301 West Jefferson Street, Suite 100, Phoenix, and is open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Maricopa County house if I owe property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax is a lien that attaches on January 1 and is paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure for your closing date, because interest keeps accruing on delinquent halves until they are paid.
